doc.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024

title: Student radio and losing the love of playing
summary: He became jazz program director on the student station and realized he did not love practicing the trumpet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: You were a kid in multiple candy shops.

It was, yeah. I mean I just — it was so lucky. But it was frustrating because I would just dive into the DownBeats and Metronones that they had in the library and I would see reviews of records that I could only dream of ever actually hearing. And I would see things written about it. And then all of a sudden when I’m able to work in this library, everything’s there. And everything that I’d ever read about or wanted to hear, there it is. And so it was. It was an amazing thing. And I continued to play — I played all the way through school. Even though I switched majors I still continued to play in the jazz bands and the concert bands and all those things. But I never loved playing like you have to love playing. And I learned that when I — it had always come pretty easy to me and I was always really good, all through school. I was always able to be in all the state bands and the whole thing. And I didn’t have to put that much effort into it. I never practiced like you were supposed to. My practice was playing along with records, and just kind of doing what I wanted to do you know. But I get to college and everybody’s as good as I am and a whole bunch of people are way better. And I’m always, I mean I’m very competitive so that wasn’t something that stopped me, but I noticed that like the people really serious lived in the practice rooms. I didn’t want to practice like that. I don’t want to practice at all. I didn’t enjoy that. I enjoyed playing in front of people. I didn’t enjoy that part of it. And at the point that I came to realize that I didn’t have the love for playing that you might need, that’s when I got more serious about this other avenue, ‘cause I fell in love with the history and the things surrounding that, the listening to the thing and all. So when I fell in love with that it gave me a clearer path. And I started telling you this because of what you asked me, which now I don’t remember, and I don’t think I answered what you had asked me, but for whatever reason it made me think of all of that. It was somehow related to what you asked me.
I don’t remember what it was.
